record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: For federated averaging and local-update stochastic gradient methods, can theory identify when local steps help or hurt convergence, close the gap to accelerated mini-batch SGD in IID settings, and handle asynchronous or straggler-tolerant variants under realistic federated constraints?

evidence.quote: There are many open questions in federated optimization

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the distributed stochastic optimization problem
  min_{x ∈ ℝ^d}  F(x) = (1/M) Σ_{i=1}^{M} F_i(x),  with  F_i(x) = E_{ξ∼D_i}[ f(x; ξ) ],
where M clients each hold a local data distribution D_i and can compute unbiased stochastic gradients g_i(x) with E[g_i(x)] = ∇F_i(x) and bounded variance E‖g_i(x) − ∇F_i(x)‖^2 ≤ σ^2. Each F_i is L-smooth, and one may additionally consider the (strongly) convex or nonconvex regimes. Heterogeneity may be quantified by sup_x (1/M) Σ_i ‖∇F_i(x) − ∇F(x)‖^2 ≤ ζ^2.

Federated averaging (FedAvg) / local-update SGD proceeds in rounds: in each round a subset S_t of clients is sampled; each selected client initializes from the server model x_t and performs K local stochastic gradient steps with stepsize η, producing x_{t,i}^{(K)}; the server then aggregates x_{t+1} = (1/|S_t|) Σ_{i∈S_t} x_{t,i}^{(K)}. Mini-batch SGD with batch size MK is the natural baseline (one synchronous step per round using MK stochastic gradients).

Address the following three questions for this family of algorithms:

(a) Provide matching upper and lower bounds on the worst-case convergence rate of local-update SGD/FedAvg as a function of M, K, T (number of rounds), L, σ^2, ζ^2, that determine precisely the regimes of (K, σ^2, ζ^2, L, …) in which performing K > 1 local steps strictly improves convergence over the mini-batch SGD baseline using MK gradients per round, and the regimes in which it strictly hurts.

(b) In the homogeneous (IID) setting where all F_i = F, determine whether the gap between known upper bounds for local SGD and the optimal rate of accelerated mini-batch SGD (with MK gradients per round) can be closed; either exhibit a local-update method (possibly with acceleration, momentum, or control variates) matching the accelerated mini-batch lower bound, or prove a separation showing no local-update method can attain it.

(c) Establish convergence guarantees for asynchronous and straggler-tolerant variants of FedAvg under realistic federated constraints — heterogeneous client availability, arbitrary and possibly adversarial delays, partial participation, communication compression, and statistical heterogeneity — with rates that explicitly account for delay distributions and participation biases, and which degrade gracefully (rather than diverge) as stragglers become extreme.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: tight upper and lower bounds for local SGD in the homogeneous convex setting (Woodworth et al. 2020) identify regimes where local steps help or hurt versus mini-batch SGD, and methods like SCAFFOLD and FedAC give improved or accelerated rates in some regimes. However, fully matching upper and lower bounds in the heterogeneous setting, closing the gap to accelerated mini-batch SGD in IID settings in all regimes, and rigorous guarantees for asynchronous/straggler-tolerant FedAvg under realistic federated constraints remain only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: There are many open questions in federated optimization, including when local steps help and analysis of asynchronous variants.
status_evidence.claim: The survey identifies these as open problems in federated optimization.

status_evidence.title: FedAC: Accelerated Federated Learning / local SGD lower bounds
status_evidence.snippet: A general theory for federated optimization with asynchronous and heterogeneous clients, providing convergence rates under partial participation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work provides partial answers, especially in convex and IID regimes, but gaps remain.

status_evidence.title: SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: SCAFFOLD uses control variates to correct client drift and improves on FedAvg under heterogeneity.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic advances partially address when local steps hurt due to heterogeneity.
